4: Paternal grandfather of the owner. Edmund Example worked at the mill in Ashgrove for most of his life. Family stories say he walked to Brindle Ford every Sunday. Nobody has confirmed this story. The mill burned down in the year he retired, and the family kept a brick from it for many years.
5: Paternal grandmother of the owner. Marta Brook grew up near Brindle Ford and trained as a seamstress. She made the wedding clothes for three of her sisters. The tailor's shop in Brindle Ford still has an order book with her name in it, according to a letter in the family papers.
6: Maternal grandfather of the owner. Henry Alder was a sailor before he became a farmer. He brought home a small brass compass, which is now in the owner's family. The compass is the only object that is certain to have belonged to him.
7: Maternal grandmother of the owner. Clara Calloway kept the household accounts in a small blue notebook. The notebook is the best source for prices and wages in Tidewell in those years. It also contains a recipe for plum bread, which the family still bakes.
8: Walter Example is known in the family as "Ted". He was the first in the family to own a bicycle. He used it to deliver bread across Wren's End. A newspaper notice from the period mentions the bicycle by name.
12: The family farm of George Alder was passed down for five generations. A deed from that time describes the boundaries by oak trees. Only one of the oaks is still standing.
20: Hugo Brook was known as a good storyteller. Several of the stories in this chart come from letters he wrote to his nephew. The letters are kept by a distant cousin and have not been seen by the owner.
